Loft: 4

Shaft Length: 33

Looks: I was very ignorant about the customization options when I first got my putter. The stock filling is the typical red and to be honest quite plain/dull. I like the simplistic look because I am not too flashy a player but, if I ever need to get a new putter, I will make sure to take advantage of some of the SC Studio options. The cover is grey and custom headcover can be bought for more $$.

Feel: The overall weight feels heavier than some of the other blades I have tried which helps me maintain a consistent path. No adjustments to the bottom weight makes the putter toe drag a bit. A solid strike with this putter feels smooth (almost as if there is no ball) and you know where the ball will be rolling. There is very little compensation on mishits though so make sure you have a reliably consistent path.

Sound: The ball sounds like butter off the sweet spot of the milled face. Some putters I have tried with inserts have a bit too much of a plastic sound for me. The lack of insert in the NP2 gives a clean solid strike sound off the sweet spot but a bit duller thud on miss hits.

Customizability: The Scotty Cameron Studio gives some of the most diverse and interesting customization options. You can easily spend your savings away with all the options

Price: Per Titleist usual it's expensive. Currently going for $350, you are mostly paying for a brand and confidence. The customization options are endless, but again you can spend everything you have on the options.
